questions.prompt: In serverless computing, which statement about servers is TRUE?
choices: You must reserve servers in advance for each function
You must patch the servers but not the applications
Servers exist, but the provider manages them
There are no servers involved anywhere in the process
questions.explanation: Serverless abstracts servers away; they still run your code, but the provider handles provisioning and maintenance.

questions.prompt: After a busy period ends, a team reduces its web tier from 8 instances to 3. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Removing instances is scaling in (horizontal); scaling down means reducing the size of an individual resource.

questions.prompt: An application depends on a web app with a 99.95% SLA and a database with a 99.99% SLA. What is the approximate composite SLA?
questions.explanation: Composite SLA = 99.95% x 99.99% = about 99.94%, which is lower than either individual SLA.

questions.prompt: What happens to an application's composite SLA as you add more services that it depends on in series?
questions.explanation: Each dependency multiplies in another chance of failure, so the composite SLA goes down.

questions.prompt: If Microsoft fails to meet the uptime in an Azure SLA, what does the customer typically receive?
choices: A full refund of all past Azure charges
An automatic upgrade to a premium tier
A service credit applied to their bill
Free hardware shipped to their datacenter
questions.explanation: Azure SLAs describe service credits as a percentage of the fee when the uptime commitment is missed.

questions.prompt: Which cloud characteristic means services are available over the network and can be used from many types of devices?
questions.explanation: Broad network access means resources are reachable over standard networks from laptops, phones and other clients.

questions.prompt: Which cloud characteristic describes a provider serving many customers from a shared pool of resources that are assigned dynamically?
questions.explanation: Resource pooling lets the provider assign physical and virtual resources to customers based on demand.

questions.prompt: A regulated organization requires that its workloads run on hardware not shared with any other organization. Which deployment model fits BEST?
questions.explanation: A private cloud is dedicated to a single organization, meeting strict single-tenant requirements.

questions.prompt: A team runs a web app on IaaS VMs and wants to reduce management overhead with minimal code changes. Which move is MOST appropriate?
choices: Add more IaaS VMs and patch them more often
Move the app to a PaaS service such as Azure App Service
Move the app back to on-premises physical servers
Move the app to larger IaaS virtual machines
questions.explanation: PaaS removes OS and runtime maintenance, reducing the work needed to run the app.

questions.prompt: In IaaS, who is responsible for the hypervisor that hosts the customer's virtual machines?
choices: Both, depending on the VM size
questions.explanation: The physical hosts and virtualization layer are managed by the cloud provider in IaaS.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between high availability and scalability?
choices: High availability lowers cost; scalability always raises cost
High availability is for storage; scalability is only for networks
High availability is about uptime; scalability is about handling load
High availability requires on-premises servers; scalability does not
questions.explanation: High availability focuses on uptime, while scalability focuses on adjusting resources to meet demand.

questions.prompt: In a hybrid cloud, how are costs typically structured?
choices: CapEx only, because cloud usage is paid up front
No costs, because the two environments offset each other
OpEx only, because hardware costs disappear entirely
CapEx for the on-premises portion and OpEx for public cloud usage
questions.explanation: The organization still buys and maintains its own hardware (CapEx) while paying for cloud consumption (OpEx).

questions.prompt: What is the main difference in tenancy between a typical public cloud and a private cloud?
choices: Public is multi-tenant; private serves one organization
Both are always single-tenant but bill in different ways
Public clouds are single-tenant; private clouds are multi-tenant
Both are always multi-tenant but use different hardware
questions.explanation: In the public cloud many customers share infrastructure with logical isolation; a private cloud is used by one organization.

questions.prompt: Which service model is MOST often licensed per user per month for a complete, ready-to-use application?
questions.explanation: SaaS applications such as Microsoft 365 are commonly priced per user subscription.

questions.prompt: A team builds an app with Azure Functions. Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the security of the function code?
choices: Nobody, because serverless code is isolated
questions.explanation: Even in serverless, the customer owns the application code and data they deploy.

questions.prompt: Which design change BEST removes a single point of failure for a web application?
choices: Increase the disk size of the single instance
Move the single instance to a larger VM size
Run at least two instances behind a load balancer
Schedule a nightly restart of the single instance
questions.explanation: Multiple instances let the app keep serving traffic if one instance fails, improving availability.

questions.prompt: A social app grows from 1,000 to 1,000,000 users over several months. Which cloud benefit allows it to keep up without buying hardware?
questions.explanation: Scalability means adding resources as demand grows, without the up-front cost of new hardware.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft guidance describes best practices for building workloads that are reliable, secure, cost-optimized, operationally excellent and performance efficient?
questions.explanation: The Well-Architected Framework is built on five pillars: reliability, security, cost optimization, operational excellence and performance efficiency.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft framework guides an organization through its cloud journey, from defining strategy and planning to governing and managing workloads?
choices: The Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure
The Total Cost of Ownership calculator
questions.explanation: The Cloud Adoption Framework covers the end-to-end adoption journey: strategy, plan, ready, adopt, govern and manage.

questions.prompt: A customer runs VMs in an Azure virtual network. Who is responsible for configuring the network security group rules for that network?
questions.explanation: In IaaS, network controls inside the customer's virtual network are configured by the customer.

questions.prompt: A QA team needs to test software on 50 different OS configurations for one afternoon. Which approach is BEST?
choices: Buy 50 physical test machines for the datacenter
Sign a three-year reservation for 50 virtual machines
Use a SaaS application instead of testing the software
Create IaaS VMs in the public cloud and delete them afterwards
questions.explanation: Public cloud IaaS lets you create many configurations quickly and pay only for the hours used.

questions.prompt: What typically distinguishes serverless compute from traditional PaaS web hosting?
choices: It always runs on a dedicated physical server for you
It is event-driven and can scale to zero, billing per execution
It can only be used from on-premises datacenters
It requires you to manage the underlying operating system
questions.explanation: Serverless services like Azure Functions run code in response to events and charge for actual executions.

questions.prompt: Which Azure service replicates virtual machines to a secondary region so they can be failed over during a disaster?
questions.explanation: Azure Site Recovery supports disaster recovery by replicating workloads and orchestrating failover.

questions.prompt: What is a limitation of relying only on vertical scaling?
choices: It always requires adding more virtual machines to a pool
You are limited by the largest available size
It can only be performed on storage accounts and disks
It removes the need for any monitoring of load
questions.explanation: Scaling up adds CPU or memory to one resource, which has an upper limit; scaling out avoids that ceiling.

questions.prompt: A company needs its VMs to keep running if one datacenter in an Azure region fails. What should it deploy the VMs across?
questions.explanation: Availability zones are physically separate locations within a region, so a zone failure does not stop VMs in other zones.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between zonal and zone-redundant Azure services?
choices: Zonal services are global; zone-redundant services exist in a single rack
Zonal services are free; zone-redundant services always need a reservation
Zonal services use one zone; zone-redundant services replicate across zones
Zonal services span regions; zone-redundant services stay in one datacenter
questions.explanation: Zonal resources such as a VM are placed in a specific zone, while zone-redundant services like ZRS storage replicate across zones for you.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a non-regional (global) Azure service?
questions.explanation: Some services such as Microsoft Entra ID, Azure DNS and Traffic Manager are not tied to a single region.

questions.prompt: How does Azure roll out planned platform updates to a region pair?
choices: Updates are applied to one region of the pair at a time
Updates are applied to both regions at the same time
Updates are never applied to paired regions
Updates are only applied to the region with less load
questions.explanation: Rolling planned updates to one region at a time minimizes downtime and the risk of both regions failing together.

questions.prompt: Azure region pairs are typically separated by at least how far?
questions.explanation: Region pairs are usually at least 300 miles apart so that a regional disaster is unlikely to affect both.

questions.prompt: In mainland China, Azure is delivered through a sovereign cloud operated by which company?
questions.explanation: Azure in China is physically separated from global Azure and operated by 21Vianet.

questions.prompt: How many levels deep can a management group hierarchy be, not counting the root level or the subscription level?
questions.explanation: A management group tree supports up to six levels of depth below the root, excluding the subscription level.

questions.prompt: A resource group is created in East US. Where can the resources inside it be located?
choices: In any region, not only East US
Only in East US and its paired region
Only in regions within the same geography
Only in East US, the group's region
questions.explanation: The resource group location stores its metadata; the resources it contains can be in different regions.

questions.prompt: A team placed a storage account in the wrong resource group. What can they do?
choices: Delete and recreate it, since resources can never move
Nest the wrong resource group inside the right one
Move the resource to another resource group
Rename the resource group to match the resource
questions.explanation: Most Azure resources can be moved between resource groups and even subscriptions.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between an Azure account and Azure subscriptions?
choices: An Azure account can have one or more subscriptions
An Azure account can have only one subscription
Subscriptions exist independently of any account
A subscription can contain multiple Azure accounts' tenants
questions.explanation: You sign up with an account and can then create multiple subscriptions for billing or access separation.

questions.prompt: What is the top-level management group in every Microsoft Entra tenant called?
questions.explanation: Every directory has a single root management group (Tenant Root Group) that all other management groups and subscriptions fall under.

questions.prompt: A company's licensing and compliance rules require its VMs to run on a physical server used only by that company. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Azure Dedicated Host provides physical servers dedicated to a single Azure subscription.

questions.prompt: When creating an Azure VM, what defines the operating system and any preinstalled software it starts with?
questions.explanation: A VM image is a template containing the OS and optionally software; the size defines CPU and memory.

questions.prompt: A company needs to run thousands of parallel, compute-intensive jobs such as rendering, with Azure managing the pool of VMs. Which service fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Azure Batch schedules and runs large-scale parallel and HPC workloads across a managed pool of VMs.

questions.prompt: A team wants to run containerized microservices with automatic scaling, including scaling to zero, without managing a Kubernetes cluster. Which service fits BEST?
choices: Azure Kubernetes Service with manual node pools
questions.explanation: Azure Container Apps is a serverless container platform that handles scaling and orchestration for you.

questions.prompt: Which Azure App Service feature lets you run background programs or scripts alongside your web app?
questions.explanation: WebJobs run background tasks in the same App Service plan as a web app.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can trigger an Azure Function to run?
choices: An HTTP request or a timer schedule
Only a change to the subscription's billing plan
Only a manual start from the Azure portal
Only a restart of the hosting virtual machine
questions.explanation: Functions run in response to triggers such as HTTP requests, timers, queue messages and other events.

questions.prompt: Compared with a virtual machine, what does a container virtualize?
choices: The physical hardware, with its own full OS
The operating system, sharing the host kernel
The network only, without any compute
The datacenter power and cooling systems
questions.explanation: VMs virtualize hardware and each runs a full OS; containers share the host OS kernel, making them lighter.

questions.prompt: A single VM's workload has grown and needs more CPU and memory. What is the quickest way to provide this?
choices: Resize the VM to a larger size
Move the VM to a different resource group
Add a tag that requests extra capacity
Apply a CanNotDelete lock to the VM
questions.explanation: Changing the VM size is vertical scaling and increases the CPU and memory available to that VM.

questions.prompt: What is the additional cost of placing VMs in an availability set?
choices: A fixed monthly fee for each availability set
No extra charge; you pay only for the VMs
A per-GB charge for replicating the VM disks
Double the price of each VM in the set
questions.explanation: Availability sets are free to configure; charges come from the VMs and other resources you deploy.

questions.prompt: Which Azure service distributes incoming network traffic across healthy VMs at the transport layer (layer 4)?
questions.explanation: Azure Load Balancer works at layer 4 (TCP/UDP); Application Gateway works at layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS).

questions.prompt: A web app needs a layer 7 load balancer that can route by URL path and includes a web application firewall. Which service fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Application Gateway is a regional layer 7 load balancer with URL-based routing and an optional WAF.

questions.prompt: Which service uses DNS to direct users to the most appropriate endpoint, such as the closest or healthiest region?
questions.explanation: Traffic Manager is a DNS-based traffic load balancer that routes clients to endpoints across regions.

questions.prompt: A global website needs edge caching, global HTTP load balancing and a web application firewall at Microsoft's network edge. Which service fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Azure Front Door combines a global layer 7 load balancer, CDN capabilities and WAF at the edge.

questions.prompt: Which Azure service is a managed, cloud-based, stateful network firewall with built-in high availability?
questions.explanation: Azure Firewall is a fully stateful firewall as a service; NSGs are simpler rule-based filters.

questions.prompt: Which VPN gateway type uses routing tables to direct packets into tunnels and is the most common choice for site-to-site connections?
questions.explanation: Route-based VPN gateways use routes to direct traffic and support most connection types, including point-to-site.

questions.prompt: Which VPN Gateway configuration improves availability by running two active instances that both maintain tunnels?
questions.explanation: In an active-active configuration both gateway instances establish tunnels, so traffic continues if one fails.

questions.prompt: A company with ExpressRoute circuits in two countries wants its on-premises sites to communicate through Microsoft's network. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: ExpressRoute Global Reach links ExpressRoute circuits to exchange data between on-premises sites.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a valid ExpressRoute connectivity model?
questions.explanation: ExpressRoute models include CloudExchange colocation, point-to-point Ethernet, any-to-any (IP VPN) and ExpressRoute Direct.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure DNS is TRUE?
choices: It only resolves names for resources outside Azure
It requires you to deploy and manage DNS servers
It hosts DNS zones but cannot buy domain names
It is the only way to register a new domain name
questions.explanation: Azure DNS hosts zones and records; registering a domain is done through a registrar.

questions.prompt: Which feature secures an Azure service such as Storage to only your virtual network by extending the VNet identity, while the service keeps its public endpoint?
questions.explanation: Service endpoints route traffic over the Azure backbone and allow the service to restrict access to your subnets.

questions.prompt: By default, can VMs in different subnets of the same virtual network communicate with each other?
choices: Yes, Azure routes between subnets by default
Yes, but only if they are in different regions
No, a VPN gateway is required between subnets
No, subnets must first be peered together
questions.explanation: Azure provides default system routes between subnets in a VNet; NSGs can restrict traffic if needed.

questions.prompt: A company wants all outbound traffic from a subnet to pass through a firewall appliance. What should it configure?
choices: A route table with user-defined routes
A tag on each virtual machine
A resource lock on the subnet
questions.explanation: User-defined routes in a route table override default routing, for example to force traffic through a firewall.

questions.prompt: VNet A is peered with VNet B, and VNet B is peered with VNet C. By default, can resources in VNet A reach VNet C?
choices: Yes, if all VNets are in one subscription
Yes, but only within the same region
questions.explanation: Peering connects only the two VNets involved; A and C need their own peering or a hub with routing.

questions.prompt: Which Blob Storage access tier sits between Cool and Archive and requires data to be kept for at least 90 days?
questions.explanation: The Cold tier is an online tier for rarely accessed data with a 90-day minimum; Cool has 30 days and Archive 180 days.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum storage duration for blobs in the Archive tier to avoid an early deletion charge?
questions.explanation: Archive data should be kept at least 180 days; deleting or moving it sooner incurs an early deletion fee.

questions.prompt: Which Blob Storage access tier can be set only on individual blobs and not as a storage account's default tier?
questions.explanation: Archive is an offline tier set at the blob level; online tiers can be used as the account default.

questions.prompt: Which blob type is optimized for append operations, such as writing log data?
questions.explanation: Append blobs are made of blocks optimized for adding data to the end, ideal for logging.

questions.prompt: Which blob type stores random-access files up to 8 TiB and is used for virtual hard disks?
questions.explanation: Page blobs support frequent random read/write operations and back VHD files.

questions.prompt: Which storage account type is recommended for most scenarios and supports blobs, files, queues and tables?
questions.explanation: Standard general-purpose v2 accounts support all core storage services and redundancy options.

questions.prompt: A workload needs high-performance, low-latency SMB and NFS file shares. Which storage account type fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Premium file share accounts use SSDs for high-performance Azure Files workloads.

questions.prompt: What is the default endpoint format for the Blob service of a storage account named contosodata?
questions.explanation: Blob endpoints follow https://<account>.blob.core.windows.net; Files uses .file.core.windows.net.

questions.prompt: What minimum durability does locally redundant storage (LRS) provide for objects over a year?
questions.explanation: LRS provides at least 11 nines; ZRS provides 12 nines; GRS and GZRS provide at least 16 nines.

questions.prompt: In geo-redundant storage (GRS), how is data copied to the secondary region?
questions.explanation: GRS replicates data to the secondary region asynchronously, so recent writes may not yet be there.

questions.prompt: With GRS but without read access enabled, when can applications read data in the secondary region?
choices: Never, the secondary copy is not readable
At any time, through a secondary endpoint
Only after a failover to the secondary region
Only during the first 30 days after creation
questions.explanation: Without RA-GRS or RA-GZRS, the secondary copy becomes accessible only after a failover.

questions.prompt: A company wants to migrate on-premises SQL Server databases to Azure SQL with minimal downtime as part of an Azure Migrate project. Which tool fits?
questions.explanation: Azure Database Migration Service migrates databases from on-premises to Azure data platforms.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum size of a single message in Azure Queue Storage?
questions.explanation: Queue Storage messages can be up to 64 KB, and a queue can hold millions of messages.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
choices: Both terms mean verifying a password and nothing more
Authentication proves who you are; authorization decides what you can access
Authentication is for apps only; authorization is for users only
Authentication decides what you can access; authorization proves who you are
questions.explanation: Authentication (AuthN) establishes identity; authorization (AuthZ) grants permissions to that identity.

questions.prompt: Help desk calls for forgotten passwords are increasing. Which Microsoft Entra feature lets users reset their own passwords securely?
questions.explanation: Self-service password reset (SSPR) lets users reset or unlock accounts after verifying their identity.

questions.prompt: A company wants administrators to activate privileged roles only when needed, for a limited time and with approval. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: PIM provides just-in-time, time-bound and approval-based activation of privileged roles.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra capability detects risks such as leaked credentials or sign-ins from unfamiliar locations?
questions.explanation: ID Protection evaluates user and sign-in risk and can feed those signals into Conditional Access.

questions.prompt: Which minimum Microsoft Entra ID edition is required to use Conditional Access?
questions.explanation: Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher; P2 adds risk-based features.

questions.prompt: A company wants to require MFA only when employees sign in from outside the corporate network. What should it configure?
questions.explanation: Conditional Access evaluates signals such as location to decide when to require MFA.

questions.prompt: An app running on an Azure VM needs to access Key Vault without storing any credentials in code. What should be used?
questions.explanation: Managed identities give Azure resources an identity in Microsoft Entra ID, with credentials managed by Azure.

questions.prompt: In Microsoft Entra ID, what is a tenant?
choices: A resource group that stores user accounts
An organization's dedicated instance of Entra ID
A single virtual machine used for sign-in
A billing invoice for identity services
questions.explanation: A tenant is an organization's dedicated Entra ID instance, created when it signs up for a Microsoft cloud service.

questions.prompt: A small company with Microsoft Entra ID Free wants a baseline of protections such as requiring MFA registration at no extra cost. What should it enable?
questions.explanation: Security defaults provide preconfigured identity protections, including MFA, for all tenants at no cost.

questions.prompt: An auditor needs to view all resources in a subscription but must not change anything. Which built-in Azure RBAC role fits BEST?
questions.explanation: The Reader role grants view access only; Contributor and Owner can make changes.

questions.prompt: Which built-in Azure RBAC role grants full access to manage all resources, including assigning roles to others?
questions.explanation: Owner has full access including role assignments; Contributor cannot grant access.

questions.prompt: Which built-in Azure RBAC role lets a user manage access for others without managing the resources themselves?
questions.explanation: User Access Administrator can manage role assignments but does not grant rights to manage resources.

questions.prompt: A user is assigned Reader at a subscription and Contributor on one resource group within it. What are the user's effective permissions on that resource group?
choices: Owner, because two roles combine into a higher role
No access, because the roles conflict
Reader, because the broader scope always wins
Contributor, because RBAC permissions are additive
questions.explanation: Azure RBAC is an allow model; effective permissions are the union of all role assignments.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is one of the three guiding principles of the Zero Trust model?
questions.explanation: Zero Trust's principles are verify explicitly, use least privilege access and assume breach.

questions.prompt: In the defense-in-depth model, which layer do network security groups and network segmentation mainly belong to?
questions.explanation: The network layer limits communication between resources through segmentation and access controls such as NSGs.

questions.prompt: In the defense-in-depth model, which layer focuses on securing VMs, for example by patching and endpoint protection?
questions.explanation: The compute layer secures access to and hardens virtual machines and other compute resources.

questions.prompt: Which defense-in-depth layer is the outermost, covering restricted building access and datacenter hardware?
questions.explanation: Physical security is the first line of defense; Microsoft secures datacenter buildings and hardware.

questions.prompt: In the defense-in-depth model, which layer is concerned with keeping applications free of vulnerabilities and storing secrets securely?
questions.explanation: The application layer integrates security into development and protects app secrets.

questions.prompt: Which environments can Microsoft Defender for Cloud protect?
choices: Only resources running inside Azure regions
Azure, on-premises, AWS and Google Cloud
questions.explanation: Defender for Cloud is a cloud-native application protection platform covering hybrid and multicloud resources.

questions.prompt: How many management groups can a single Microsoft Entra directory support?
questions.explanation: A directory can contain up to 10,000 management groups.

questions.prompt: A subscription can trust how many Microsoft Entra tenants at a time for authentication?
questions.explanation: Each subscription is associated with a single Microsoft Entra tenant, though a tenant can have many subscriptions.

questions.prompt: A team wants to deploy a new version of an App Service web app to staging, test it, then swap it into production with no downtime. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: Deployment slots are live apps with their own hostnames that can be swapped into production.

questions.prompt: When you create an Azure VM in the portal, which resources are typically created with it?
choices: A new subscription and a tenant
A management group and a policy
A Key Vault and an ExpressRoute circuit
A network interface and an OS disk
questions.explanation: A VM relies on supporting resources such as a NIC, managed disks and usually a virtual network and public IP.

questions.prompt: How many VPN gateways can a single Azure virtual network have?
questions.explanation: Each virtual network can have only one VPN gateway, though it can support multiple connections.

questions.prompt: An NSG is applied to a subnet and only the default rules exist. What happens to inbound traffic from the internet?
choices: It is denied by a default rule
It is allowed on all ports by default
It is redirected to Azure Firewall
It is allowed only on ports 80 and 443
questions.explanation: Default NSG rules allow traffic within the VNet and from the Azure load balancer, and deny other inbound traffic.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Entra ID edition includes ID Protection and Privileged Identity Management?
questions.explanation: P2 includes everything in P1 plus ID Protection and Privileged Identity Management.

questions.prompt: Which hybrid identity sign-in method synchronizes a hash of users' on-premises password hashes to Microsoft Entra ID?
questions.explanation: Password hash sync lets users sign in to cloud services with the same password; pass-through validates against on-premises AD instead.

questions.prompt: Which current Microsoft product name covers identity for external users, including business partners and customers of your apps?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra External ID brings B2B collaboration and customer identity (CIAM) under one product.

questions.prompt: Which Defender for Cloud feature keeps VM management ports such as RDP closed until a user requests access for a limited time?
questions.explanation: Just-in-time VM access reduces exposure by opening management ports only when approved and only temporarily.

questions.prompt: How can the subscription type affect what you pay for Azure services?
choices: Some subscription types include usage allowances that offset costs
Subscription type only affects the color scheme of the portal
Every subscription type has exactly the same pricing and benefits
Subscription type determines which regions exist on the planet
questions.explanation: Subscriptions such as the free account or dev/test offers include allowances or discounts that change your costs.

questions.prompt: A company buys a third-party firewall appliance from the Azure Marketplace. How is it typically billed?
choices: It is always free because it runs on Azure
Directly by cash payment to the vendor's local office
Through a separate Microsoft 365 license invoice
questions.explanation: Marketplace solutions are billed through Azure and may include the vendor's software fees plus the Azure resources used.

questions.prompt: A company's Azure bill rises as it streams large video files from Azure to internet users. Which charge is MOST likely growing?
questions.explanation: Data leaving Azure datacenters is generally billed, while most inbound data transfer is free.

questions.prompt: Which statement about data transfer between two Azure regions is TRUE?
choices: Traffic between regions is generally charged
Traffic between regions is always free
Only inbound internet traffic between regions is billed
Regions cannot exchange any data at all
questions.explanation: Inter-region data transfer, including traffic over global VNet peering, incurs charges.

questions.prompt: In the TCO calculator, which assumptions can you adjust to reflect your on-premises environment?
choices: Costs such as electricity and IT labor
The Azure Policy effects applied to resources
The Azure SLA percentage for each service
The number of availability zones in a region
questions.explanation: The TCO calculator lets you change assumptions like electricity cost and IT labor rates to compare more accurately.

questions.prompt: Do you need an Azure subscription to use the Azure pricing calculator?
choices: Yes, and it requires an Enterprise Agreement
No, it is freely available on the web
Yes, only Owners of a subscription can use it
No, but it only works for on-premises servers
questions.explanation: The pricing calculator is a public tool for estimating costs before you deploy anything.

questions.prompt: Which Cost Management alert type notifies you when a department's spending in an Enterprise Agreement reaches a fixed threshold of its quota?
questions.explanation: Department spending quota alerts are configured in the EA portal and trigger when a department reaches a quota threshold.

questions.prompt: Besides sending email, what can an Azure budget alert do when a threshold is reached?
choices: Trigger an action group that runs automation
Automatically move resources to a cheaper region
Delete the subscription to prevent further charges
questions.explanation: Budgets can be linked to action groups to run automation like runbooks or functions when costs hit a threshold.

questions.prompt: A team creates a budget for its subscription. When spending exceeds the budget, what happens by default?
choices: The subscription is disabled until next month
New deployments are blocked by the budget
An alert is sent, but resources keep running
questions.explanation: Budgets notify you; they do not stop resources unless you add automation through action groups.

questions.prompt: A company runs various compute services and wants a discount by committing to a fixed hourly spend for one or three years, without locking into a specific VM size or region. What fits BEST?
choices: Azure Reservations for a specific VM size
questions.explanation: A savings plan applies a committed hourly spend across eligible compute services, giving more flexibility than reservations.

questions.prompt: Which term lengths are available when purchasing Azure Reservations?
questions.explanation: Reservations are purchased for one-year or three-year terms in exchange for a discount.

questions.prompt: How long does the starting credit included with an Azure free account last?
questions.explanation: The free account includes credit for the first 30 days, plus some services free for 12 months and others always free.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum number of tag name-value pairs a single Azure resource can have?
questions.explanation: Each resource, resource group or subscription can have up to 50 tag name-value pairs.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure tags is TRUE?
choices: Not all resource types support tags
Tags can only be added when a resource is created
Tags are required on every resource by default
questions.explanation: Most resource types support tags, but not all; tags can be added or changed after creation.

questions.prompt: A team tags VMs with Shutdown=19:00 so that a script can find and stop them each evening. Which use of tags is this?
questions.explanation: Tags can drive automation, letting scripts identify which resources to act on.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the case sensitivity of Azure tags is TRUE?
choices: Names are case-sensitive; values are case-insensitive
Both names and values are case-insensitive
Both names and values must be uppercase
Names are case-insensitive; values are case-sensitive
questions.explanation: Azure treats tag names as case-insensitive for operations, while tag values are case-sensitive.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid storing sensitive information such as passwords in tags?
choices: Tags are deleted automatically after 24 hours
Tags cause resources to become publicly accessible
Tags are plain text visible to many users and in reports
Tags are limited to numbers and cannot hold text
questions.explanation: Tag data is not protected like secrets and appears in places such as billing data; use Key Vault for secrets.

questions.prompt: After its initial evaluation, how often does Azure Policy run a standard compliance evaluation cycle on assigned scopes?
choices: Only when an admin requests it
questions.explanation: Policy evaluates on create or update, on new assignment, and in a standard compliance scan every 24 hours.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Policy effect deploys a related resource, such as diagnostic settings, when it is missing?
questions.explanation: DeployIfNotExists runs a template deployment to add a missing related resource, often via a remediation task.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Policy effect can add, update or remove tags on a resource during creation or update?
questions.explanation: The Modify effect changes properties such as tags on resources; Deny blocks and Audit only reports.

questions.prompt: A policy is assigned to a subscription, but one resource group must be excluded from evaluation. What should the administrator configure?
choices: A tag named Exclude on the subscription
A new tenant for that resource group
An exclusion or exemption for that group
A ReadOnly lock on that resource group
questions.explanation: Policy assignments support exclusions, and exemptions can waive evaluation for specific scopes.

questions.prompt: In which format are Azure Policy definitions written?
questions.explanation: Policy definitions are JSON documents that describe conditions and the effect to apply.

questions.prompt: A company wants to be alerted to existing storage accounts that allow non-HTTPS traffic, without blocking any deployments. What should it use?
choices: An Azure budget with an email alert
An Azure Policy assignment with the Audit effect
A Contributor role assignment for auditors
A CanNotDelete lock on each storage account
questions.explanation: Audit reports non-compliant resources without preventing them from being created.

questions.prompt: A company must measure its Azure environment against a standard such as NIST SP 800-53. What is the QUICKEST way to start?
choices: Apply ReadOnly locks to every subscription
Assign the built-in compliance initiative for it
Write hundreds of custom policies from scratch
Create a tag named NIST on each resource
questions.explanation: Azure Policy includes built-in regulatory compliance initiatives that group the relevant policies.

questions.prompt: By default, which built-in roles can create or delete management locks?
choices: Any user who can view the resource
questions.explanation: Creating or deleting locks requires Microsoft.Authorization/locks permissions, held by Owner and User Access Administrator.

questions.prompt: At which scopes can Azure resource locks be applied?
questions.explanation: Locks can be set on subscriptions, resource groups and resources; child scopes inherit them.

questions.prompt: A CanNotDelete lock is applied to a storage account. Can a user with appropriate data permissions still delete blobs inside it?
choices: No, the lock makes all blobs read-only
No, the lock blocks every delete within the account
Yes, but only after the lock expires in 24 hours
Yes, locks protect management operations only
questions.explanation: Locks apply to control plane operations; deleting blobs is a data plane operation and is not blocked.

questions.prompt: A company wants to protect sensitive information in Microsoft 365 services such as Teams, OneDrive and Exchange, for example with data loss prevention. Which solution family fits?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview includes information protection and data loss prevention for Microsoft 365 data.

questions.prompt: Data analysts need a place to discover trusted, well-described data sources across the organization. Which Microsoft Purview capability fits?
questions.explanation: Purview's catalog lets users search and understand registered data assets and their classifications.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Azure PowerShell is TRUE?
choices: It can only be used inside the Azure portal
It runs only on Windows Server
It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux
It manages Microsoft 365 but not Azure
questions.explanation: The Az PowerShell module runs on PowerShell 7 across Windows, macOS and Linux, as well as in Cloud Shell.

questions.prompt: How is the Azure portal maintained by Microsoft?
choices: It is updated once a year with a new version
Each customer must install updates manually
It goes offline every weekend for updates
It is updated continuously without downtime
questions.explanation: The portal is a web-based console that Microsoft updates continuously without maintenance downtime.

questions.prompt: An ARM template creates a VM that must wait until its virtual network exists. Which ARM capability handles this?
choices: Tagging both resources with the same value
Creating the VM in a different subscription
Applying a CanNotDelete lock to the virtual network
questions.explanation: Resource Manager uses declared dependencies to order deployments, running independent resources in parallel.

questions.prompt: How can a large ARM template be broken into smaller, reusable components?
choices: By assigning each section a different tag
By using linked or nested templates
By splitting it across multiple Azure regions
By converting it into a PowerShell runbook
questions.explanation: Linked and nested templates (or Bicep modules) let you build deployments from reusable parts.

questions.prompt: What happens to a Bicep file when it is deployed to Azure?
choices: It is compiled into a Windows executable on each VM
It is run as a shell script inside Cloud Shell only
It is stored as a tag on the target resource group
It is converted into an ARM JSON template first
questions.explanation: Bicep is a language that transpiles to ARM JSON, so it has the same capabilities as ARM templates.

questions.prompt: When an on-premises server is connected with Azure Arc, how does it appear in Azure?
choices: As a brand new Azure subscription
As a Microsoft Entra user account
As an Azure resource in a resource group
As a blob inside a storage account
questions.explanation: Arc-enabled servers are projected into Azure Resource Manager so they can be tagged, governed and managed like Azure resources.

questions.prompt: What is an advantage of using Azure Cloud Shell instead of installing the Azure CLI locally?
choices: It lets you manage Azure without any Azure account
It runs offline without an internet connection
It is the only tool that can create virtual machines
It runs in the browser with tools preinstalled
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell is browser-based, includes Azure CLI and PowerShell, and authenticates with your portal account.

questions.prompt: A team uses an open-source, third-party infrastructure as code tool that works across Azure and other clouds. Which tool is this MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Terraform is a popular third-party IaC tool that supports Azure; Bicep is Microsoft's Azure-specific language.

questions.prompt: Azure Advisor recommends adding a second instance to a single VM to meet an SLA. Which Advisor category is this?
questions.explanation: Reliability recommendations help ensure continuity of business-critical applications.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Advisor category includes recommendations about process and workflow efficiency, resource manageability and deployment best practices?
questions.explanation: Operational excellence recommendations focus on efficient processes, manageability and deployment practices.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants to be notified before planned maintenance affects services in their subscriptions. What should they configure?
questions.explanation: Service Health alerts notify you about service issues, planned maintenance and advisories that affect your resources.

questions.prompt: Azure Monitor collects two fundamental types of data. How do metrics differ from logs?
choices: Metrics are kept forever; logs are deleted every hour
Metrics are text messages; logs are numeric counters only
Metrics are numeric time series; logs are event records
Metrics come from on-premises only; logs come from Azure only
questions.explanation: Metrics are lightweight numeric time series; logs contain detailed records that can be queried.

questions.prompt: Where does Azure Monitor store log data so that it can be queried with KQL?
questions.explanation: Logs are collected into Log Analytics workspaces and analyzed with Kusto Query Language.

questions.prompt: Which Application Insights feature periodically sends requests to a website from locations around the world to check that it responds?
questions.explanation: Availability tests are synthetic checks that monitor uptime and responsiveness from multiple locations.

questions.prompt: In Azure Monitor, what is an action group?
choices: A set of RBAC roles assigned to a resource group
Notification preferences and actions used by alerts
A group of VMs that share an availability set
A bundle of policies that enforce compliance
questions.explanation: Action groups define who is notified and what automation runs, such as email, SMS, webhooks or runbooks.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Monitor feature provides a ready-made view of VM performance and the dependencies between VMs and other systems?
questions.explanation: VM insights monitors VM health and performance and can map processes and dependencies.

questions.prompt: An admin wants a resource's platform logs sent to a Log Analytics workspace and a storage account for archiving. What should be configured?
choices: A CanNotDelete lock on the resource
A tag named Logs on the resource
questions.explanation: Diagnostic settings route platform logs and metrics to destinations such as Log Analytics, Storage or Event Hubs.

questions.prompt: By default, how long does Azure retain Activity log events?
questions.explanation: Activity log entries are kept for 90 days; send them to a Log Analytics workspace or storage for longer retention.

questions.prompt: Which agent is the current recommended way to collect monitoring data from the guest OS of VMs for Azure Monitor?
questions.explanation: The Azure Monitor Agent replaces the retired legacy Log Analytics agent for collecting guest data.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Monitor feature provides flexible, interactive reports that combine text, metrics and log queries into one visual canvas?
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor workbooks create rich interactive reports from multiple data sources.

questions.prompt: A finance analyst needs to view and analyze Azure cost data but must not manage any resources. Which built-in role fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Cost Management Reader can view cost data and configuration without permission to change resources.

questions.prompt: A company wants to prevent anyone from creating public IP addresses in a subscription. What should it use?
choices: Azure Policy with a Deny effect
questions.explanation: Azure Policy can deny the creation of specific resource types; locks only protect existing resources from deletion or change.

questions.prompt: A team deleted a VM but still sees storage charges for it. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The VM's managed disks were not deleted with it
Deleted VMs are still billed for compute hours
Azure Policy evaluations incur a per-VM charge
The resource group charges a monthly fee
questions.explanation: Deleting a VM does not always delete its disks, NICs or public IPs, which may keep generating charges.

questions.prompt: Which tool provides a compliance score and recommended improvement actions to help an organization meet regulations such as GDPR?
questions.explanation: Compliance Manager assesses your controls against regulations and suggests improvement actions.

questions.prompt: A developer with a Visual Studio subscription wants discounted rates for non-production workloads. Which offer fits BEST?
choices: Azure Spot Virtual Machines for production
questions.explanation: Azure Dev/Test pricing provides discounted rates for development and test workloads for Visual Studio subscribers.

questions.prompt: Which section of an ARM template lets you supply values, such as VM size or region, at deployment time?
questions.explanation: Parameters let the same template be reused with different values for each environment.

questions.prompt: Which command signs you in to Azure using the Azure CLI?
questions.explanation: az login authenticates the Azure CLI; Connect-AzAccount is the Azure PowerShell equivalent.

questions.prompt: Which cmdlet signs you in to Azure using Azure PowerShell?
questions.explanation: Connect-AzAccount authenticates an Azure PowerShell session.

questions.prompt: Which PowerShell module is the current, recommended module for managing Azure resources?
questions.explanation: The Az module replaces the retired AzureRM module for managing Azure resources.

questions.prompt: How much does it cost to use Azure Advisor?
choices: A percentage of total Azure spending
It is free, with no additional charge
A fixed monthly fee per subscription
questions.explanation: Azure Advisor is a free service that analyzes your resource configuration and usage.

questions.prompt: An admin wants to quickly plot a chart of a VM's CPU percentage over the last 24 hours in the portal. Which Azure Monitor tool fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Metrics explorer lets you interactively chart and compare metric values for resources.

questions.prompt: At which scopes can you create a budget in Microsoft Cost Management?
choices: A subscription or a resource group, among others
Only an individual virtual machine disk
Only a Microsoft Entra user account
questions.explanation: Budgets can be created at scopes including billing accounts, management groups, subscriptions and resource groups.

questions.prompt: In the Azure portal, how are the two resource lock types displayed?
choices: Freeze for CanNotDelete, and Lock for ReadOnly
Protect for CanNotDelete, and Block for ReadOnly
Delete for CanNotDelete, and Read-only for ReadOnly
Archive for CanNotDelete, and Seal for ReadOnly
questions.explanation: The portal shows CanNotDelete as Delete and ReadOnly as Read-only.

questions.prompt: Which Azure scopes can have tags applied?
choices: Only Microsoft Entra users and groups
questions.explanation: Tags can be applied to resources, resource groups and subscriptions.

questions.prompt: In Azure Resource Manager, what supplies resource types such as Microsoft.Compute and Microsoft.Storage?
questions.explanation: Resource providers are services that offer resource types; they must be registered in a subscription.

questions.prompt: What is the default deployment mode for an ARM template deployment to a resource group?
choices: Partial, which deploys only the first resource listed
Incremental, which leaves other resources alone
Complete, which deletes resources not in the template
Preview, which never makes any changes to Azure
questions.explanation: Incremental mode adds or updates resources; complete mode removes resources that are not in the template.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is an event type shown in Azure Service Health?
questions.explanation: Service Health reports service issues, planned maintenance, health advisories and security advisories.

questions.prompt: A finance team wants Azure cost data automatically saved as a file to a storage account every day for its own reporting tools. What should it configure?
choices: A CanNotDelete lock on the storage account
A scheduled export in Cost Management
questions.explanation: Cost Management exports can deliver cost data to a storage account on a daily, weekly or monthly schedule.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Arc capabilities for servers are available at no extra cost?
choices: Unlimited data ingestion into Log Analytics
All Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans for the servers
Free Windows Server licenses for every server
Control plane features such as inventory and tagging
questions.explanation: Azure Arc control plane functionality is free; add-on services such as Defender or Monitor are billed separately.

questions.prompt: Before deploying a Bicep or ARM template, which operation lets you preview the changes it would make to existing resources?
questions.explanation: What-if shows which resources would be created, changed or deleted without actually deploying.

questions.prompt: When persistent storage is mounted in Azure Cloud Shell, where are your files kept across sessions?
choices: In the Activity log of the subscription
In a Microsoft Entra user attribute
In an Azure file share in a storage account
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell can mount an Azure Files share so files persist between sessions.

questions.prompt: In Azure App Service, what determines the region, the number of VM instances and the size of the compute resources that web apps run on?
questions.explanation: An App Service plan defines the set of compute resources (region, instance count, size and pricing tier) that one or more apps run on. Deployment slots are just separate instances of an app for staging.

questions.prompt: A company wants users to sign in without a password by approving a notification on their phone and entering a matching number shown on screen. Which passwordless method fits?
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Authenticator app supports passwordless phone sign-in with number matching. Windows Hello for Business uses biometrics or a PIN tied to a specific PC, and SMS codes are not passwordless.

questions.prompt: Factory workers share computers and are not allowed to carry phones on the production floor. Which passwordless sign-in method is MOST appropriate?
questions.explanation: FIDO2 security keys are portable hardware authenticators that work on shared devices without needing a phone. The other options all depend on a mobile phone.

questions.prompt: A company wants employees to access corporate email only from devices that are marked as compliant in its device management system. What should it configure?
choices: An Azure Policy assignment with the Deny effect on mailboxes
A network security group rule on the email server subnet
A resource lock on the mailbox resources
A Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant device
questions.explanation: Conditional Access can use device state as a signal and grant access only when the device is marked compliant. Azure Policy and resource locks govern Azure resources, not user sign-ins.

questions.prompt: None of the built-in Azure RBAC roles match the exact set of permissions a team needs. What should an administrator do?
choices: Create an Azure custom role with only the required actions
Assign the Owner role and ask the team to be careful
Apply a ReadOnly resource lock to the subscription
Create a new Microsoft Entra tenant for the team
questions.explanation: When built-in roles are too broad or too narrow, you can create custom roles that list exactly the allowed actions, supporting least privilege.

questions.prompt: Using just-in-time and just-enough access, and risk-based adaptive policies, to limit what users can do supports which Zero Trust principle?
questions.explanation: Zero Trust's 'use least privilege access' principle limits user access with JIT/JEA and risk-based adaptive policies. 'Verify explicitly' is about always authenticating and authorizing using all available signals.

questions.prompt: Which security standard does Microsoft Defender for Cloud assess resources against by default to generate its security recommendations?
questions.explanation: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is the default standard in Defender for Cloud; other regulatory standards such as PCI DSS or NIST can be added to the compliance dashboard.

questions.prompt: An administrator tries to peer two virtual networks that both use the 10.0.0.0/16 address space. What will happen?
choices: Peering succeeds but only for traffic on port 443
Peering succeeds and Azure translates the overlapping addresses automatically
Peering succeeds only after a VPN gateway is deployed into each virtual network
Peering fails, because peered networks cannot have overlapping address spaces
questions.explanation: Virtual network peering requires non-overlapping IP address spaces. Readdressing one network is needed before the peering can be created.

questions.prompt: A large enterprise wants to connect directly to Microsoft's global network at a peering location at 10 or 100 Gbps, without going through a connectivity provider. Which option fits?
questions.explanation: ExpressRoute Direct provides dual 10 Gbps or 100 Gbps physical ports directly into Microsoft's network at peering locations. Standard ExpressRoute circuits are usually provisioned through a connectivity provider.

questions.prompt: How are network security group (NSG) rules evaluated for a packet?
choices: Deny rules are always evaluated after every allow rule has been checked
By priority, lowest number first, stopping at the first matching rule
All matching rules are combined and the most permissive rule always wins
In alphabetical order of rule name
questions.explanation: NSG rules are processed by priority number, with lower numbers first. Once traffic matches a rule, processing stops, so later rules are not evaluated.

questions.prompt: An application needs zone redundancy in the primary region, replication to a secondary region and the ability to read from the secondary region at any time. Which redundancy option fits?
choices: Zone-redundant storage (ZRS) in the primary region
questions.explanation: RA-GZRS combines ZRS in the primary region with geo-replication and read access to the secondary region. GRS without read access only allows reads after a failover.

questions.prompt: Financial records in Blob Storage must not be modified or deleted by anyone for seven years to meet a regulatory requirement. Which feature should be used?
choices: Geo-redundant storage with read access enabled
questions.explanation: Immutable storage puts blobs in a write-once, read-many (WORM) state for the retention period. Soft delete only allows recovery for a limited time and does not prevent deletion.

questions.prompt: A user accidentally deleted several blobs yesterday. Which feature, if enabled beforehand, lets the administrator recover them within a configured retention period?
questions.explanation: Blob soft delete keeps deleted blobs for a set retention period so they can be restored. Geo-replication copies deletions to the secondary region as well.

questions.prompt: A partner needs read access to one blob for the next 24 hours without being given the storage account keys. What is the MOST appropriate solution?
choices: Give the partner the storage account access key
Generate a shared access signature (SAS) that expires in 24 hours
Assign the partner the Owner role on the subscription
Make the container public for one day and then make it private again
questions.explanation: A SAS grants limited, time-bound permissions to specific storage resources without exposing account keys. Account keys and the Owner role grant far more access than needed.

questions.prompt: Which hybrid identity sign-in method validates users' passwords directly against on-premises Active Directory at sign-in time, using an agent, without storing password hashes in the cloud?
questions.explanation: Pass-through authentication uses on-premises agents to validate passwords against Active Directory in real time. Password hash synchronization stores a hash of the password hash in Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.prompt: Managers must periodically confirm that their team members still need membership in groups that grant access to sensitive apps. Which Microsoft Entra feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Access reviews let reviewers regularly attest whether users still need group memberships, application access or role assignments, and remove access that is no longer needed.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Microsoft Entra roles and Azure RBAC roles is TRUE?
choices: Entra roles manage directory objects; Azure roles manage Azure resources
Azure RBAC roles are the only way to manage users and licenses in Entra ID
They are the same roles shown in two places in the portal
Entra roles can only be assigned at the resource group scope
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra roles (such as Global Administrator or User Administrator) control directory objects, while Azure RBAC roles (such as Owner or Contributor) control Azure resources at management group, subscription, resource group or resource scope.

questions.prompt: What is an Azure geography?
choices: A single datacenter with its own independent power, cooling and network
A market with one or more regions that keeps data residency boundaries
A billing boundary for a set of resource groups
A group of availability zones within one region
questions.explanation: Geographies such as 'Europe' or 'Japan' contain one or more regions and help customers meet data residency, sovereignty and compliance requirements.

questions.prompt: An IoT analytics application writes very large numbers of small objects to Blob Storage and needs consistently low latency for these operations. Which storage account type is the BEST fit?
choices: Standard general-purpose v2 with the Cool tier
Standard general-purpose v2 with the Archive tier
questions.explanation: Premium block blob storage accounts use SSDs and are designed for high transaction rates and low, consistent latency with block blobs. Page blobs are for random read/write workloads like VM disks.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Cost Management feature can notify a team when spending in a subscription suddenly deviates from its usual pattern, even if no budget has been exceeded?
questions.explanation: Cost Management can detect cost anomalies based on historical usage and send anomaly alerts. Budget alerts only fire at fixed thresholds you define.

questions.prompt: A company wants documents labeled 'Confidential' to stay encrypted and access-restricted wherever they are shared, including outside the organization. Which Microsoft Purview capability fits?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels classify content and can apply protection such as encryption that travels with the file. Tags and locks apply only to Azure resources, not documents.

questions.prompt: An ARM template is deployed to a resource group in complete mode. What happens to existing resources in the group that are NOT defined in the template?
choices: They are locked with a ReadOnly lock
They are moved to a new resource group
questions.explanation: Complete mode makes the resource group match the template, deleting resources not in it. The default incremental mode leaves such resources unchanged.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants to be notified whenever anyone deletes a virtual machine in a production subscription. Which type of Azure Monitor alert fits BEST?
choices: A metric alert on VM CPU percentage
An activity log alert on the VM delete operation
An Application Insights availability test on the VM's public endpoint
questions.explanation: Deleting a VM is a control-plane operation recorded in the activity log, so an activity log alert can fire on that event. Metric alerts track numeric performance values.

questions.prompt: After a service outage last month, an administrator wants to read the post-incident review Microsoft published for issues that affected the subscription. Where should they look?
choices: Health history in Azure Service Health
questions.explanation: Azure Service Health keeps a health history of past service issues affecting your subscriptions, including downloadable post-incident reviews.

questions.prompt: An administrator needs to quickly query and inventory resources across dozens of subscriptions, for example listing all VMs without a backup tag. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Azure Resource Graph lets you run fast, KQL-based queries over resource properties at scale across subscriptions and management groups.

questions.prompt: A company buys an Azure Reservation for VMs and sets its scope to Shared. How is the discount applied?
choices: Only to VMs in the resource group where it was bought
Automatically to matching resources in eligible subscriptions
Only after each VM is manually linked to the reservation by an administrator
Only to the single VM chosen at purchase time
questions.explanation: With a shared scope, the reservation discount applies automatically to matching resources across eligible subscriptions in the billing account or context; no manual assignment to individual VMs is needed.

questions.prompt: A company runs the same VM size in the same region 24/7 and expects no changes for three years. Compared with an Azure savings plan for compute, why might Azure Reservations be preferred?
choices: Reservations can be cancelled for a full refund at any time
Reservations also cover all Azure Marketplace software licenses automatically, at no cost
Reservations usually give a deeper discount for steady use of specific resources
Reservations are the only option that supports a three-year term
questions.explanation: Savings plans trade some discount for flexibility across sizes and regions, while reservations usually give the highest savings when usage of a specific resource type and region is steady.

questions.prompt: Two VMs have the same size and region, but one runs Windows Server and the other Linux. Why is the Windows VM typically more expensive on pay-as-you-go pricing?
choices: Windows VMs are placed in more availability zones
Windows VMs always use premium storage
Linux VMs are not billed for compute time
Its price includes the Windows Server license
questions.explanation: Windows VM pricing includes the operating system license unless Azure Hybrid Benefit is applied with eligible existing licenses.

questions.prompt: A developer wants a visual diagram showing the components of a distributed web application and the dependencies, failures and latency between them. Which Application Insights feature fits?
questions.explanation: Application map in Application Insights shows the components of an application and the calls between them, highlighting performance bottlenecks and failure hotspots.

questions.prompt: Where do the security recommendations shown in Azure Advisor come from?
questions.explanation: Advisor's security category surfaces recommendations from Microsoft Defender for Cloud, giving a single place to view recommendations across all categories.

questions.prompt: What is installed on an on-premises Windows or Linux server so it can be onboarded as an Azure Arc-enabled server?
questions.explanation: The Azure Connected Machine agent connects a server to Azure Arc, after which it appears as an Azure resource that can be governed with Azure Policy, RBAC and tags.

questions.prompt: A new Azure Policy assignment with the Deny effect blocks VMs without a required tag. What happens to existing VMs that were created earlier without the tag?
choices: They are moved to a quarantine resource group
They are stopped until the tag is added
They keep running and are reported as non-compliant
questions.explanation: The Deny effect prevents new non-compliant creates and updates; existing resources are not deleted or stopped but show as non-compliant in the compliance results.

questions.prompt: Which section of an ARM template returns values, such as a newly created resource's endpoint, after deployment finishes?
questions.explanation: The outputs section returns values from a deployment. Parameters supply values at deployment time, and variables hold values reused within the template.

questions.prompt: Which Azure CLI command creates a new resource group?
questions.explanation: In the Azure CLI, 'az group create' with a name and location creates a resource group. New-AzResourceGroup is the Azure PowerShell equivalent.

questions.prompt: A company wants to know whether buying Azure Reservations would save money based on its actual VM usage over recent weeks. Which free tool provides personalized reservation recommendations?
questions.explanation: Azure Advisor's cost recommendations include reservation purchase suggestions based on your usage history, along with rightsizing and shutdown recommendations.

questions.prompt: An administrator needs a single assignment that checks a set of related rules, such as required tags and allowed locations, across many subscriptions under a management group. What is the MOST efficient approach?
choices: Create a custom RBAC role for each rule
Create a resource lock on each subscription
Assign each policy definition separately to every resource group in each subscription
Assign an initiative of the policies at the management group
questions.explanation: An initiative groups related policy definitions so they are assigned and tracked together, and assigning it at a management group applies it to every subscription below.

questions.prompt: A company runs all of its servers in its own on-premises datacenter. Who is responsible for the physical security of that datacenter?
choices: Responsibility is shared equally with Microsoft
questions.explanation: In an on-premises datacenter the organization owns every layer, including physical security. Moving to the cloud shifts physical security to the provider.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for network controls in a SaaS offering such as Microsoft 365?
choices: Shared equally between customer and Microsoft
questions.explanation: For SaaS, the provider manages network controls along with the application, OS and infrastructure. Network controls are the customer's in IaaS and shared in PaaS.

questions.prompt: A business states that it can afford to lose at most 15 minutes of data after a disaster. Which metric does this define?
questions.explanation: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time. RTO is the maximum acceptable time to restore service.

questions.prompt: Management requires that the order system be running again within two hours of any major outage. Which metric does this describe?
questions.explanation: RTO is the target maximum time allowed to restore a service after an interruption. RPO concerns how much data can be lost.

questions.prompt: A government agency must keep certain citizen data inside its own country, where no Azure region exists, but wants to use Azure for its public website. Which deployment model fits BEST?
questions.explanation: A hybrid model keeps regulated data in the agency's own datacenter while using Azure for workloads without residency restrictions.

questions.prompt: A service has a monthly SLA of 99.95%. Approximately how much downtime does this allow in a 30-day month?
questions.explanation: A 30-day month has 43,200 minutes; 0.05% of that is about 21.6 minutes. About 4 minutes corresponds to 99.99%, and about 44 minutes to 99.9%.

questions.prompt: In the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure, which methodology focuses on preparing the cloud environment, such as building landing zones, before workloads are migrated?
questions.explanation: The Ready methodology prepares the environment for adoption, typically by deploying Azure landing zones. Adopt covers migrating and innovating, and Manage covers ongoing operations.

questions.prompt: What is an Azure landing zone?
choices: A peering location where ExpressRoute circuits from providers terminate
A region reserved for disaster recovery failover
A single virtual machine used to test new applications
A prepared environment with identity, networking and governance in place
questions.explanation: An Azure landing zone is a scalable, well-governed foundation, including subscription organization, identity, networking and policies, prepared before workloads are deployed.

questions.prompt: A team load-tests its application and configures autoscaling so it meets changing demand without overprovisioning. Which Azure Well-Architected Framework pillar is it addressing?
questions.explanation: Performance Efficiency is about a workload's ability to scale and meet demand efficiently. Reliability focuses on resilience and recovery from failures.

questions.prompt: Why is the cloud often a more cost-effective option for disaster recovery than building a second on-premises datacenter?
choices: Disaster recovery is included free of charge with every Azure subscription
No idle second site to buy; you pay mostly for replication until failover
Data never needs to be copied when using the cloud
Cloud providers guarantee that disasters will never affect any region at all
questions.explanation: Using another Azure region for DR removes the cost of a second physical site; services such as Azure Site Recovery replicate data and you scale up compute only when failing over.

questions.prompt: A company needs a higher SLA for a single Azure VM but cannot add more instances. Which change can raise the VM's single-instance SLA?
choices: Moving the VM to a different resource group
Applying a CanNotDelete lock to the VM
Using Premium SSD or Ultra Disk for all of its disks
Adding tags that mark the VM as a critical production workload
questions.explanation: Microsoft's single-instance VM SLA depends on disk type, with the highest single-VM SLA requiring Premium SSD or Ultra Disk for all OS and data disks. Resource groups, locks and tags do not affect availability.

questions.prompt: A defense agency needs to run a subset of Azure services in its own datacenter, including in locations that may be disconnected from the internet. Which offering is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Azure Stack Hub extends Azure services into an organization's own datacenter and can operate in disconnected scenarios, supporting hybrid cloud requirements.

questions.prompt: A team rightsizes underused VMs and shuts down development resources at night to avoid waste. Which Azure Well-Architected Framework pillar does this support?
questions.explanation: Cost Optimization focuses on avoiding unnecessary expense, for example by rightsizing resources and turning off what is not being used.

questions.prompt: A team uses automated, repeatable deployment pipelines and monitoring so it can release changes safely and detect problems quickly. Which Azure Well-Architected Framework pillar does this support?
questions.explanation: Operational Excellence covers the operations processes that keep a workload running in production, such as DevOps practices, automated deployments and monitoring.

questions.prompt: A company runs a database engine that it installed itself on an Azure virtual machine. Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for applying updates to that database engine?
choices: The database vendor, because it supplies the update files
Microsoft, because database patching is always a provider task
The customer, because it installed and manages the software on the VM
Microsoft, because the VM runs on Azure hardware
questions.explanation: On IaaS, any software the customer installs on the VM, including a database engine, is the customer's to patch. Microsoft patches the engine only in PaaS offerings such as Azure SQL Database.

questions.prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, how is responsibility for network controls typically divided in a PaaS deployment?
choices: It belongs to the customer's internet provider
It is shared between the customer and Microsoft
It belongs entirely to the customer
questions.explanation: Microsoft's shared responsibility model shows network controls as a customer task in IaaS, shared in PaaS and a Microsoft task in SaaS.

questions.prompt: Which on-premises cost is an operational expenditure (OpEx) rather than a capital expenditure (CapEx)?
choices: Purchasing new rack servers for the datacenter
Buying network switches and firewalls outright
The monthly electricity bill for the server room
questions.explanation: Recurring bills for services consumed, such as electricity, are OpEx. Buying servers, switches or buildings is up-front CapEx that is depreciated over time.

questions.prompt: An Azure service automatically replaces an unhealthy instance after a health probe fails, without any administrator action. This is an example of which aspect of cloud manageability?
questions.explanation: Management of the cloud covers automatic scaling, template-based deployment, health monitoring with automatic replacement and alerts. Management in the cloud is how you manage resources, such as through the portal, CLI or APIs.

questions.prompt: Which of the following Azure services is an example of infrastructure as a service (IaaS)?
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual Machines give you control of the OS and installed software, which is IaaS. App Service and Functions are PaaS or serverless, and Microsoft 365 is SaaS.

questions.prompt: A company deploys two independent instances of an application, each with 99% availability, so that the application stays up as long as at least one instance is running. What is the approximate combined availability?
questions.explanation: With redundant instances in parallel, the chance both are down is 0.01 x 0.01 = 0.0001, giving about 99.99%. Multiplying 0.99 x 0.99 (98.01%) applies only to services that depend on each other in series.

questions.prompt: A service has an SLA of 99% uptime. Approximately how much downtime does this allow in a 30-day month?
questions.explanation: 1% of a 30-day month (720 hours) is 7.2 hours. 43 minutes corresponds to 99.9%, and 22 minutes to 99.95%.

questions.prompt: A service has an SLA of 99.99% uptime. Approximately how much downtime does this allow over a full year?
questions.explanation: 0.01% of 8,760 hours is about 0.876 hours, or roughly 53 minutes. About 8.8 hours per year corresponds to 99.9%.

questions.prompt: A team designs its workload to encrypt data, apply least-privilege access and detect threats. Which pillar of the Azure Well-Architected Framework is it mainly addressing?
questions.explanation: The Security pillar covers protecting confidentiality, integrity and availability through controls such as encryption, least privilege and threat detection.

questions.prompt: A team adds health probes, redundancy across availability zones and a tested failover plan so its workload can recover from failures. Which Azure Well-Architected Framework pillar does this mainly support?
questions.explanation: Reliability is about a workload being resilient and able to recover from failures, which redundancy, health probes and failover plans support.

questions.prompt: In the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure, which methodology focuses on defining the business justification and expected outcomes of moving to the cloud?
