questions.explanation: The Strategy methodology captures motivations, business outcomes and the business case. Ready prepares the environment, Adopt covers migration and innovation, and Manage covers operations.

questions.prompt: A company resizes a running Azure VM from a small size to a much larger size to handle more load. What should the team typically expect during the change?
choices: The VM is deleted and must be redeployed
A second VM is added behind a load balancer
The VM restarts, causing a brief interruption
The VM keeps running with no interruption
questions.explanation: Scaling a single VM up or down changes its hardware allocation, which requires a restart. Adding another VM behind a load balancer would be scaling out, not resizing.

questions.prompt: A company plans to scale its web tier out to many identical instances behind a load balancer. Which application design makes this work BEST?
choices: A single instance that holds all user sessions
Instances that each store sessions on their own disk
Instances that each use a different code version
Instances that keep no user session state locally
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling works best when any instance can handle any request, so session state should be kept outside the individual instances, for example in a shared cache or database.

questions.prompt: A company moves its email from on-premises Exchange servers to Exchange Online in Microsoft 365. Who is now responsible for replacing failed server hardware?
choices: The hardware manufacturer, through the company
questions.explanation: Exchange Online is SaaS, so Microsoft owns and maintains all the underlying infrastructure, including server hardware.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes a limitation of the public cloud compared with a private cloud?
choices: Less control over the hardware and its configuration
The organization maintains the physical datacenter
Hardware must be bought up front before scaling
Paying only for resources used is not possible
questions.explanation: In the public cloud the provider owns the hardware, so customers do not have full control over it. Up-front hardware purchases and datacenter upkeep are drawbacks of a private cloud.

questions.prompt: An accounting firm's website traffic is extremely high from January to April and low the rest of the year. Which approach BEST controls cost while keeping the site responsive?
choices: Buy enough on-premises servers to handle the April peak each year
Configure autoscaling so capacity follows demand through the year
Run a single small instance all year and accept slower performance
Run the peak number of instances all year to be safe from slowdowns
questions.explanation: Autoscaling uses the cloud's elasticity to add capacity during busy months and remove it afterwards, so the firm pays only for what it needs.

questions.prompt: A finance manager wants to forecast cloud spending accurately before deploying a new project. Which cloud benefit does this relate to?
questions.explanation: Cost predictability is about forecasting spending, supported by tools such as the pricing calculator and Cost Management. Performance predictability is about meeting expected performance, for example through autoscaling.

questions.prompt: A small business wants to use the cloud but has no IT staff to patch servers, operating systems or applications. Which service model requires the LEAST management effort from it?
choices: A private cloud on its own hardware
questions.explanation: With SaaS the provider runs and patches the whole application stack; the customer mainly manages its data, users and devices.

questions.prompt: A developer builds an Azure Functions app that resizes photos when they are uploaded to a storage account. Under the shared responsibility model, who is responsible for the servers that run the function?
questions.explanation: Azure Functions is serverless, so Microsoft provisions, patches and scales the underlying servers. The developer remains responsible for the function code and data.

questions.prompt: Which characteristic distinguishes a hybrid cloud from a multi-cloud setup?
choices: Hybrid uses only private cloud resources in several datacenters
Hybrid combines on-premises or private infrastructure with public cloud
Hybrid uses two or more public cloud providers together
Hybrid is a single public cloud spread across many regions
questions.explanation: A hybrid cloud connects private or on-premises infrastructure with a public cloud. Using multiple public cloud providers is multi-cloud.

questions.prompt: A media company needs extra rendering capacity for a two-month project. Compared with buying servers, which benefit does the cloud's consumption-based model provide?
choices: It requires a long-term contract that lowers the hourly price
It lets the company depreciate the servers over five years
It avoids up-front hardware costs and charges only for the time used
It guarantees the hardware remains available after the project
questions.explanation: Consumption-based pricing has no up-front cost and bills only for resources used, so short-term needs do not require buying hardware.

questions.prompt: In the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure, which methodology covers building an inventory of the digital estate and creating a skills readiness plan for the cloud adoption?
questions.explanation: The Plan methodology turns the strategy into an actionable plan, including rationalizing the digital estate and planning skills readiness.

questions.prompt: A company runs a Windows Server VM in Azure and needs to restrict which ports are open in the operating system's own firewall. Under the shared responsibility model, who configures this?
choices: The customer, because the guest OS is under its control
The customer's internet provider, as the network carrier
Microsoft, because Azure configures VM firewalls by default
Microsoft, because it manages the hypervisor and hosts
questions.explanation: In IaaS the customer controls the guest operating system, including its host firewall settings. Microsoft is responsible for the physical hosts and hypervisor beneath the VM.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the cloud's security benefit is TRUE?
choices: Customers can pick a service model for the level of control they want
The provider is responsible for classifying the customer's data
Moving to the cloud removes every security task from the customer
Customers must patch the operating system of every cloud service
questions.explanation: IaaS gives maximum control over security configuration, while PaaS and SaaS hand more tasks, such as patching, to the provider. Data classification always stays with the customer.

questions.prompt: A company considers moving a workload from an on-premises virtual machine to a PaaS service. Which responsibility would it STOP having after the move?
questions.explanation: In PaaS the provider manages the operating system. Data, accounts and identities, and devices remain the customer's responsibility in every model.

questions.prompt: A company wants to back up its Azure virtual machines daily and keep recovery points for several months so it can restore a VM after accidental changes. Which service should it use?
questions.explanation: Azure Backup creates scheduled backups with retained recovery points for restores. Azure Site Recovery replicates workloads for disaster recovery failover rather than long-term backup retention.

questions.prompt: When Azure Backup protects Azure VMs, which resource stores the backup data and backup policies?
questions.explanation: Azure VM backups are stored and managed in a Recovery Services vault, which also holds the backup policies. Key Vault stores secrets and keys, not backups.

questions.prompt: A development team builds Docker images and needs a private, Azure-hosted place to store and manage them so that AKS can pull them. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Azure Container Registry is a managed, private registry for container images. Azure Container Instances runs containers but does not act as an image registry.

questions.prompt: How many IP addresses does Azure reserve in each subnet of a virtual network, which cannot be assigned to resources?
questions.explanation: Azure reserves five addresses in every subnet: the network address, the broadcast address and three addresses used for the default gateway and Azure DNS.

questions.prompt: A network security group can be associated with which Azure resources?
questions.explanation: An NSG filters traffic when it is associated with a subnet, a VM's network interface, or both.

questions.prompt: An administrator wants NSG rules that allow traffic to 'all web servers' without listing each server's IP address, so new web VMs are covered automatically when added to the group. What should be used?
questions.explanation: Application security groups let you group VMs by role and reference that group in NSG rules instead of individual IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A company connects its datacenter to Azure with ExpressRoute and wants a lower-cost backup path in case the ExpressRoute circuit fails. What is a common solution?
choices: Global virtual network peering to another region
A point-to-site VPN from one administrator laptop
A second availability set in the same region
A site-to-site VPN connection as a failover path
questions.explanation: A site-to-site VPN over the internet can be configured alongside ExpressRoute as a backup connection for the same on-premises network.

questions.prompt: A company's datacenter is located in a colocation facility that also hosts a cloud exchange. Which ExpressRoute connectivity model is MOST likely to be used?
questions.explanation: With the CloudExchange colocation model, a company in a facility with a cloud exchange orders virtual cross-connections to the Microsoft cloud through the exchange provider.

questions.prompt: VMs in a private subnet have no public IP addresses but need outbound internet access to download updates, using a fixed set of public IPs. Which service fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Azure NAT Gateway provides outbound-only internet connectivity for a subnet using static public IPs. Bastion provides inbound admin access, and Private Link connects privately to services.

questions.prompt: A three-tier application needs to distribute traffic from its web tier to several application-tier VMs that have only private IP addresses. Which option fits BEST?
questions.explanation: An internal (private) load balancer distributes traffic inside a virtual network to back-end VMs with private IPs. Traffic Manager and Front Door are for internet-facing, global routing.

questions.prompt: A company has dozens of branch offices worldwide and wants a Microsoft-managed networking service that connects branches, VPN users and Azure virtual networks through hubs. Which service fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Azure Virtual WAN is a managed networking service that brings together branch connectivity, VPN, ExpressRoute and VNet connectivity through Microsoft-managed hubs.

questions.prompt: What is the correct hierarchy for storing objects in Azure Blob Storage?
choices: Blob, then container, then storage account
Resource group, then blob, then container
Storage account, then container, then blob
Container, then storage account, then blob
questions.explanation: A storage account contains containers, and each container holds blobs, similar to folders holding files.

questions.prompt: A data engineering team needs Blob Storage with a hierarchical namespace for big data analytics workloads. Which capability should it use?
choices: Azure managed disks on Premium SSD
questions.explanation: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 is built on Blob Storage and adds a hierarchical namespace optimized for analytics.

questions.prompt: A test VM must run as cheaply as possible and its disk performance is not important. Which managed disk type is the MOST cost-effective?
questions.explanation: Standard HDD disks are the lowest-cost option and suit dev/test and non-critical workloads. Premium SSD and Ultra Disk cost more for higher performance.

questions.prompt: A mission-critical database on an Azure VM needs the highest disk throughput and IOPS with sub-millisecond latency. Which managed disk type fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Ultra Disks offer the highest IOPS and throughput with very low latency for data-intensive workloads such as top-tier databases.

questions.prompt: A company must keep its data in a single Azure region for data residency reasons, but the data must survive the loss of an entire datacenter in that region. Which redundancy option fits BEST?
questions.explanation: ZRS copies data across three availability zones in one region, surviving a datacenter failure without copying data to another region. LRS keeps all copies in one datacenter, and GRS replicates to a second region.

questions.prompt: Why does every Azure storage account have two access keys?
choices: So one key is used for blobs and the other for files
So one key is used for reads and the other for writes
So each key is used in a different Azure region
So keys can be rotated without interrupting applications
questions.explanation: Two keys let you switch applications to the second key, regenerate the first, and repeat, rotating keys without downtime.

questions.prompt: Users sometimes overwrite important documents in Blob Storage. Which feature automatically keeps earlier versions of a blob each time it is modified?
questions.explanation: Blob versioning automatically saves the previous state of a blob whenever it is overwritten or deleted so it can be restored.

questions.prompt: A company wants to host a simple static website made of HTML, CSS and image files directly from a storage account. Which container serves the site's files?
questions.explanation: When static website hosting is enabled on a storage account, Azure creates a container named $web that serves the site's content.

questions.prompt: An administrator cannot mount an Azure file share over SMB from an on-premises Windows server. Which outbound port is MOST likely blocked by the company firewall?
questions.explanation: Mounting an Azure file share with SMB requires outbound TCP port 445, which many organizations and ISPs block.

questions.prompt: In Microsoft Entra ID, which object represents an application's identity in a tenant so the app can be granted access to resources?
questions.explanation: A service principal is the identity of an application or service in a tenant, used to assign it roles and permissions. Managed identities are a special kind of service principal managed by Azure.

questions.prompt: Several VMs and an App Service app must all use the same identity to access a storage account, and the identity must keep existing even if one of those resources is deleted. Which option fits BEST?
choices: A system-assigned managed identity on each resource
A personal user account for the app team
A shared storage account access key
questions.explanation: A user-assigned managed identity is a standalone Azure resource that can be attached to many resources and has its own lifecycle. A system-assigned identity is tied to one resource and is deleted with it.

questions.prompt: A company wants users to be added to and removed from a Microsoft Entra group automatically based on their Department attribute. What should it use?
choices: A group with dynamic membership rules
A security group with assigned membership
questions.explanation: Dynamic membership groups evaluate user attributes, such as department, and update membership automatically. Assigned groups require manual changes.

questions.prompt: A company wants to synchronize users from several disconnected on-premises Active Directory forests to Microsoft Entra ID using lightweight provisioning agents managed from the cloud. Which tool fits BEST?
choices: Azure Active Directory B2C user flows
questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync uses lightweight agents with configuration held in the cloud, and it supports syncing from multiple disconnected forests. Domain Services provides managed domains, not synchronization.

questions.prompt: A company already runs an on-premises federation server, such as AD FS, and requires that all sign-in validation, including smart card authentication, happens on-premises. Which hybrid identity sign-in method fits?
questions.explanation: With federation, Microsoft Entra ID hands authentication to the on-premises federation service, so validation and requirements such as smart card sign-in are handled on-premises. Password hash synchronization validates sign-ins in the cloud.

questions.prompt: A user signs in by scanning a fingerprint. Which category of authentication factor is this?
questions.explanation: Biometrics such as fingerprints or face recognition are 'something you are'. A password is something you know, and a phone or security key is something you have.

questions.prompt: A company wants a Conditional Access policy to block sign-ins from countries where it has no employees. What should it define first so the policy can reference those countries?
questions.explanation: Named locations define IP ranges or countries that Conditional Access policies can include or exclude as a condition.

questions.prompt: An Azure RBAC role assignment is made up of which three elements?
choices: A policy definition, an initiative and an assignment
A tag name, a tag value and a resource
A security principal, a role definition and a scope
A user, a password and a subscription
questions.explanation: A role assignment attaches a role definition (what can be done) to a security principal (who) at a scope (where).

questions.prompt: A company's policy is to authenticate and authorize every access request using all available signals, such as user identity, location and device health. Which Zero Trust principle does this reflect?
questions.explanation: Verify explicitly means always authenticating and authorizing based on all available data points. Assume breach is about minimizing blast radius, and least privilege about limiting access.

questions.prompt: In the defense-in-depth model, at which layer would you place Azure Firewall and DDoS protection that filter attacks before they reach your network?
questions.explanation: The perimeter layer uses DDoS protection and perimeter firewalls to filter large-scale attacks before they cause a denial of service for users.

questions.prompt: A company wants Microsoft Defender for Cloud to provide threat detection and alerts for its servers and storage accounts, beyond the free posture recommendations. What should it enable?
choices: Azure Advisor cost recommendations for storage
Microsoft Entra Connect Health on every server
The relevant Defender plans, such as Defender for Servers
Azure Policy remediation tasks for each subscription
questions.explanation: Defender plans provide cloud workload protection, such as threat detection for servers or storage. The free foundational posture management offers recommendations and secure score.

questions.prompt: Which Microsoft Defender for Cloud capability is available at no extra cost?
choices: Defender for Storage malware scanning on uploads
Just-in-time VM access for every VM in Azure
Defender for Servers threat detection on all VMs
questions.explanation: Foundational CSPM, which provides security recommendations and secure score, is free. Workload protections such as Defender for Servers, which includes just-in-time access, are paid plans.

questions.prompt: An organization needs keys stored in Azure Key Vault to be protected by hardware security modules (HSMs). Which option meets this requirement?
choices: The Key Vault Premium tier or Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
The Key Vault Standard tier with software-protected keys
Storing the keys as secrets in an App Service configuration
Azure Storage Service Encryption with Microsoft-managed keys
questions.explanation: Key Vault Premium supports HSM-protected keys, and Managed HSM provides a fully managed, single-tenant HSM pool. The Standard tier protects keys with software only.

questions.prompt: A company has not purchased any DDoS protection plan. What DDoS protection do its Azure resources have?
choices: Full DDoS Network Protection with cost protection guarantees
Protection only for resources hosted in Azure Government
Default infrastructure-level protection from the platform
No protection at all until a DDoS plan has been purchased
questions.explanation: Every Azure property gets default platform-level DDoS infrastructure protection at no cost. DDoS Network Protection and DDoS IP Protection add tuned mitigation, telemetry and other features for a fee.

questions.prompt: A company plans a disaster recovery design that relies on Azure region pairs. Which fact about region pairs should it keep in mind?
choices: Every Azure region has exactly two paired regions
Paired regions must always be in different geographies
Some newer Azure regions do not have a paired region
Region pairs can be chosen by each customer
questions.explanation: Microsoft defines region pairs, and some newer regions are not paired and rely on availability zones instead. Most pairs are in the same geography.

questions.prompt: Which Azure region is a well-known exception because it is paired with a region OUTSIDE its own geography?
questions.explanation: Brazil South is paired with South Central US, outside its geography. Most region pairs, such as East US and West US, stay within the same geography.

questions.prompt: An administrator tries to create a resource group inside an existing resource group to organize resources further. What happens?
choices: It works, but the child group inherits all the parent's resources
It is not possible, because resource groups cannot be nested
It works, and up to six levels of nesting are allowed
It works, but only in the same region
questions.explanation: Resource groups are a flat container and cannot be nested. Management groups, not resource groups, support a nested hierarchy.

questions.prompt: A web app on Azure App Service needs more memory per instance and access to features available only in a higher pricing tier. What should the administrator do?
choices: Create a deployment slot for the app
Move the app to a different resource group
Scale up by moving the App Service plan to a higher tier
Scale out by adding more instances in the same tier
questions.explanation: Scaling up changes the App Service plan's pricing tier, giving more CPU, memory and features. Scaling out adds instances but keeps the same per-instance resources and features.

questions.prompt: A company wants to run an existing SQL Server workload in Azure with nearly 100% compatibility with on-premises SQL Server, without managing the operating system. Which service fits BEST?
choices: SQL Server on an Azure virtual machine
questions.explanation: Azure SQL Managed Instance is a PaaS offering with near-complete SQL Server engine compatibility. SQL Server on a VM is also compatible, but the customer manages the OS.

questions.prompt: A developer wants a VM to be directly accessible from the internet for testing. Which resource must be associated with its network interface?
questions.explanation: A public IP address associated with a VM's network interface (or a load balancer) lets it be reached from the internet. Private DNS zones and route tables do not provide internet reachability.

questions.prompt: A team adds several VMs and a database to an estimate in the Azure pricing calculator. What happens in the team's Azure subscription?
choices: The resources are deployed in a stopped state
A budget is created automatically for the estimate
The resources are reserved at the estimated price
Nothing is created; it only produces an estimate
questions.explanation: The pricing calculator is an information-only tool for estimating costs. It does not provision anything or lock in prices.

questions.prompt: A team wants a Cost Management budget to warn it when spending is PROJECTED to exceed the budget before the month ends, not only after it actually does. What should it configure?
choices: A Service Health alert for the subscription
An Azure Policy with the Audit effect
A resource lock on the subscription
A budget alert based on forecasted cost
questions.explanation: Cost Management budgets can trigger alerts on actual cost or on forecasted cost, so teams can act before an overspend happens.

questions.prompt: The operations team tags resources with Impact=mission-critical so it can prioritize them during incidents. Which tagging use case is this?
questions.explanation: Tags that describe business criticality help operations teams prioritize work and set availability expectations. Cost-center tags support cost management, and Confidentiality tags support security.

questions.prompt: Which Azure Policy effect flags VMs as non-compliant when a related resource, such as a required VM extension, does NOT exist, without deploying anything?
questions.explanation: AuditIfNotExists audits when a related resource is missing. DeployIfNotExists would deploy the missing resource, and Deny blocks creation.

questions.prompt: A company wants to ensure that only approved resource types, such as VMs, storage accounts and virtual networks, can be created in a subscription. What is the MOST direct approach?
choices: Assign the built-in Allowed resource types policy
Apply a ReadOnly lock to the whole subscription
Create a separate budget for each resource type
Tag every resource with its approved resource type
questions.explanation: The built-in Allowed resource types policy denies deployment of any resource type not on the approved list. Locks block changes to existing resources, not types.

questions.prompt: A ReadOnly lock is applied to a storage account. A developer then cannot retrieve the account's access keys in the portal. Why?
choices: Listing keys is a POST operation, which the lock blocks
ReadOnly locks hide the storage account from users
The lock removed the developer's RBAC role assignment
ReadOnly locks delete the account's access keys
questions.explanation: A ReadOnly lock blocks all operations other than reads. Listing storage keys uses a POST request, so it is blocked even though it seems like a read.

questions.prompt: An administrator tries to delete a resource group, but one storage account inside it has a CanNotDelete lock. What happens?
choices: Everything except the locked storage account is deleted
The lock is removed automatically and everything is deleted
Only the locked storage account is deleted
questions.explanation: A lock on any resource within a resource group prevents the resource group from being deleted, because deleting the group would delete the locked resource.

questions.prompt: A ReadOnly lock is applied to a resource group that contains virtual machines. What is a likely side effect?
choices: The VMs are stopped and deallocated immediately
Users cannot start or restart the VMs
The VMs can still be resized but not deleted
The VMs can be deleted by Owners only
questions.explanation: Starting or restarting a VM uses a POST request, which a ReadOnly lock blocks. This is why ReadOnly locks can have unexpected effects.

questions.prompt: Which document explains what personal data Microsoft collects, how it uses that data and for what purposes?
questions.explanation: The Microsoft Privacy Statement describes the personal data Microsoft processes, how it processes it and why. SLAs describe uptime commitments, not privacy.

questions.prompt: An ARM template must create a management group hierarchy and assign policies across several subscriptions. Which statement about ARM template deployment scope is TRUE?
choices: They can be deployed only through the Azure portal by a user with the Owner role
They can target resource group, subscription, management group or tenant scope
They can be deployed only at the subscription scope and only in a single region
They can be deployed only to one resource group at a time, never to higher scopes
questions.explanation: Azure Resource Manager supports deployments at the resource group, subscription, management group and tenant scopes, from the portal, CLI, PowerShell or pipelines.

questions.prompt: A team writes Bicep code and wants to reuse a standard virtual network definition across many deployments. Which Bicep feature supports this?
questions.explanation: Bicep modules let you package resources into a separate file and reuse them from other Bicep files. Initiatives group Azure Policy definitions, not templates.

questions.prompt: A platform team wants to store approved ARM templates in Azure so other teams can deploy them, with access controlled by Azure RBAC. Which feature fits?
questions.explanation: Template specs store ARM templates (or Bicep compiled to them) as Azure resources that can be shared and secured with RBAC.

questions.prompt: A company onboards on-premises Windows servers to Azure Arc. Which capability does this enable?
choices: Converting the servers automatically into Azure SQL databases
Moving the servers' physical hardware into an Azure region
Running the servers without any operating system installed
Protecting the servers with Microsoft Defender for Cloud
questions.explanation: Arc-enabled servers are projected into Azure, so services such as Azure Policy, Azure Monitor and Microsoft Defender for Cloud can manage and protect them where they run.

questions.prompt: An administrator decides that an Azure Advisor recommendation does not apply right now but may matter later. What can the administrator do with it?
choices: Assign it as an Azure Policy initiative
Convert it into a resource lock
questions.explanation: Advisor lets you postpone a recommendation for a period or dismiss it, so it no longer appears in the active list.

questions.prompt: What severity levels can be assigned to Azure Monitor alert rules?
questions.explanation: Azure Monitor alerts use five severity levels from Sev 0, Critical, to Sev 4, Verbose.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants to stop Azure Monitor alert notifications from firing during a planned weekend maintenance window, without disabling the alert rules. What should it use?
choices: An alert processing rule that suppresses notifications
A Cost Management budget with a zero spending threshold
An Azure Policy assignment that uses the Deny effect
A CanNotDelete lock applied to each of the alert rules
questions.explanation: Alert processing rules can suppress action groups for fired alerts during a scheduled window, such as planned maintenance.

questions.prompt: Auditors need to review subscription activity log events from the past year, but the activity log keeps events for only 90 days by default. What should the administrator do?
choices: Apply a ReadOnly lock to the subscription to preserve the activity log
Send the activity log to Log Analytics or storage with a diagnostic setting
Enable Azure Service Health alerts to archive past activity events
Raise the Azure Advisor score so that older events are kept longer
questions.explanation: Sending the activity log through a diagnostic setting to Log Analytics or a storage account keeps the data beyond the default 90-day retention.

questions.prompt: Which activity log category records create, update and delete operations performed through Azure Resource Manager?
questions.explanation: The Administrative category contains all create, update, delete and action operations performed through Resource Manager.

questions.prompt: A network administrator wants to check whether a network security group rule is blocking traffic from a VM to a specific IP address and port. Which Azure Network Watcher tool fits?
questions.explanation: IP flow verify tests whether a packet to or from a VM is allowed or denied and reports which NSG rule made the decision.

questions.prompt: A company wants one service to assess and install operating system updates for its Azure VMs and its Azure Arc-enabled servers on-premises, on a schedule. Which service fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Azure Update Manager manages and schedules OS updates for Windows and Linux machines in Azure, on-premises and in other clouds through Azure Arc.

questions.prompt: A team wants to run a scheduled PowerShell script in Azure every evening to stop development VMs, without maintaining a server to run it. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: Azure Automation runs PowerShell or Python runbooks on a schedule in the cloud, which is commonly used to stop and start VMs.

questions.prompt: Besides the 30-day starting credit, what does an Azure free account include?
choices: Unlimited free use of every Azure service for one full year
A free dedicated host for running production workloads
Popular services free for 12 months, plus always-free services
Free Azure Reservations for three years on any VM size
questions.explanation: The Azure free account combines a 30-day credit with certain popular services free for 12 months and other services that are always free within limits.

questions.prompt: A university student wants to learn Azure without entering a credit card. Which offer is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Azure for Students provides credit and free services to verified students without requiring a credit card. Dev/Test pricing requires a Visual Studio subscription.

questions.prompt: Is there an extra charge for using Microsoft Cost Management to analyze and manage Azure costs?
choices: Yes, it requires a separate monthly license
Yes, it is charged by the number of resources analyzed
Yes, it is charged per budget created
No, it is available for Azure at no additional cost
questions.explanation: Microsoft Cost Management is included at no additional cost for managing Azure spending.

questions.prompt: A company runs Red Hat Enterprise Linux VMs in Azure and already has eligible Red Hat subscriptions. Which benefit can reduce its costs by applying those existing subscriptions?
questions.explanation: Azure Hybrid Benefit applies to Windows Server and SQL Server licenses and also to eligible RHEL and SLES subscriptions, so you avoid paying twice for the software.

questions.prompt: An organization wants to audit settings inside the operating system of its VMs, such as whether a specific application is installed, using Azure Policy. Which capability makes this possible?
choices: Azure Service Health alerts for each subscription
Cost Management exports to a storage account
Azure Resource Graph queries across subscriptions
questions.explanation: Azure Machine Configuration extends Azure Policy to audit or configure settings inside the guest operating system of Azure and Arc-enabled machines.

questions.prompt: An AKS team wants ready-made monitoring of cluster, node and container performance and logs in Azure Monitor. Which feature fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Container insights is the Azure Monitor feature that collects and visualizes performance and log data from AKS and other Kubernetes clusters.

questions.prompt: A developer wants to start collecting Application Insights telemetry from a web app. What are the typical ways to enable it?
choices: Assign the Reader role to the web app's identity
Enable autoinstrumentation or add the SDK to the app
Create a budget for the web app's resource group
Apply a CanNotDelete resource lock to the web app
questions.explanation: Application Insights can be enabled through autoinstrumentation for supported hosting environments, or by adding the SDK to the application code.

questions.prompt: A company wants every resource deployed through Azure Resource Manager to be manageable as a group, so it can deploy, update and delete all resources of an application together. Which ARM concept supports this?
choices: Placing the application's resources in the same resource group
Applying the same tag value to resources in different tenants
Purchasing an Azure Reservation that covers the application
Creating a separate Microsoft Entra tenant for the application
questions.explanation: Resource Manager lets you manage resources in a resource group as a unit, so resources that share a lifecycle can be deployed, updated and deleted together.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants an alert whenever a specific error message appears in application logs collected in a Log Analytics workspace. Which type of Azure Monitor alert fits BEST?
choices: A metric alert on CPU percentage
A log search alert using a KQL query
questions.explanation: Log search alerts run a KQL query against log data on a schedule and fire when results match, such as a particular error text. Metric alerts evaluate numeric metrics instead.

questions.prompt: A company wants to apply Azure Policy and monitoring to Kubernetes clusters running in its own datacenter and in another cloud. What should it use?
choices: Azure Kubernetes Service in a new region
questions.explanation: Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes connects clusters running anywhere to Azure so they can be governed with Azure Policy, monitored and configured with GitOps.

questions.prompt: A company wants to use one Azure Policy definition for allowed locations, but with West Europe allowed for one subscription and East US for another. How can this be done without writing two definitions?
choices: Create a resource lock with the location in its name
Move both subscriptions into a single management group
Use parameters and supply different values per assignment
Apply a different tag to each of the two subscriptions
questions.explanation: Policy definitions can expose parameters, such as a list of allowed locations, so the same definition can be assigned with different values at different scopes.

questions.prompt: An administrator wants to be notified automatically whenever Azure Advisor generates a new recommendation for a subscription. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: Advisor alerts notify you, through action groups, when new recommendations of the selected category or impact are generated.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants to find notices about upcoming retirements of Azure features its resources use, so it can plan changes. Which type of Azure Service Health event should it look at?
questions.explanation: Health advisories cover changes that need attention, such as feature retirements and breaking changes. Service issues describe current outages.

questions.prompt: An administrator leaves an Azure Cloud Shell session idle. Approximately how long does the session last without interactive activity before it times out?
questions.explanation: Cloud Shell sessions end after about 20 minutes without interactive activity; files in mounted storage persist for the next session.
